chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Willard on his playing; the Ellington album track "Orson" and Kenny Burrell
summary: They discuss Jones's playing on Ellington tribute albums made with Kenny Burrell and the chemistry of the sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I'll remember that. Now, you do something very special that there's nobody else does it quite like you do. And that's why you're where you are and who you are.
Pat, do you know that to me -- I don't know, let's see. To me it's just --

When you sit down at the piano some very beautiful things come out and they're unique. Nobody else plays them. They don't occur to anybody else. I mean have you listened to your, "Orson," on Ellington's record.

Yeah, I did. Because a lot of times I do things that I'm not -- I say, "Gee, I could have done this that way or this way." You know. You hear -- you always hear something else you might have done, in retrospect, you know. But I liked it. I sat there last night and just put it on and I put it on where it would repeat that whole last side, starting with -- that's a good album.
It sure is a good album.
You know, I listened to the whole thing. That's a good album. I think I like some of the things in this one better than I do the last one.
But there are some very exciting things happening here.
Because I talked with Kenny about it, you know, and I said, "Kenny how does it sound?" I'm more
interested in how the music sounds. How did it come off? He says it's good, man. Just like that.
Yeah, Kenny was very happy with it.
Yeah. Well, we had so much stored up. From the first album, that we could always use it for the second one.
Yeah. It was such good things. I mean we only intended to do enough material for one album the first time, but there was nothing that could be discarded out of it.
No, there was too many great musicians and too much -- I guess it was just that the chemistry was there. And I have to agree with you.
